newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Danubius prospers as city hotels outdo spa.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Danubius prospers as city hotels outdo spa.

text.p: Danubius Hotels said on Friday a reduced dependence on its spa operations and increased occupancy rates of its Budapest hotels had contributed to a 40 percent increase in its January to September consolidated pre-tax profit.

"Unlike the past few years when...our hotels other than in Budapest achieved comfortably higher occupancy rates, (this year) our Budapest hotels proved 1.3 percentage points better on average," the company said in its results report.
"This was caused mainly by the booming business of Budapest's tourism industry this year and some large-scale contracts providing steady occupancies," the company said.

Figures released on Friday showed the group posted a consolidated pre-tax profit of 2.273 billion forints, 40.2 percent up on the same period of last year and above the entire 1995 pre-tax profit of 2.057 billion forints.
Operating profits rose 39.6 percent to 2.073 billion forints while net sales grew 39.1 percent to 7.69 billion forints as average occupancy rates rose to 69.9 percent.
The steady occupancy contracts included a deal to offer facilities to U.S. troops on leave from the U.S. Army's forward base for the Bosnian peace implementation force at Taszar in southern Hungary.

Danubius has traditionally been a provider of spa medical facilities to customers from Austria and Germany, who come to four spa hotels at the eastern end of Lake Balaton in western Hungary. Such trade accounts for around 50 percent of its business.

On September 30, Danubius signed a contract with the State Privatisation Agency to buy 85 percent of hotel chain Hungaria Szalloda Rt for over eight billion forints. The transaction has yet to be approved by the government's Competition Office.
Danubius shares on Friday soared to an all-time high of 3,560 on the news of the results before falling back in a bout of profit-taking to 3,275, down 175 on the day.
